feature: Building with components, from a blank canvas to a change carried everywhere
summary: You can draw a control by hand, turn it into a component, decide which three things about it a copy may change, give it a second look called Disabled, place copies that follow it, change one of them and put that change straight back, place a copy that arrives already Disabled, and then edit the original once and carry that edit to every version. This is the whole path in one sitting, not eight features side by side.
setup: Photonz Dev, Experiments window, release Next. Components, versions, knobs and the Library are all on by default. Start from a blank canvas, 1440 by 1024.

try.do: Press R and drag a box about 360 by 120, then drag a corner handle in to round it. Press T, click inside the box and type Save.
Press V, drag a marquee round both, press Command G, type 16 into Padding, then rename the group Save button.
Press Option Command K. The Library opens with a Save button tile on it.
In the Component section press Add and pick Text “Save” under Wording. Do it twice more for Rectangle · Corner radius and Save button · Padding, naming them Corner radius and Room.
Press Add beside Versions, call the new drawing Disabled, and drop its opacity so the two differ.
Drag the Save button tile onto the canvas three times.
Click the middle copy, type Cancel into Label, then type 48 into Room. Press the way-back arrow beside each to undo them one at a time.
Click the tile, set Place to Disabled, and drag one more copy out: it arrives already faded.
Click a copy, press Edit Original, turn Shadow on for the box inside it, then press Apply to Disabled.

evaluate: Is this the order you would do it in, or would you add the second version before you ever thought about knobs?
The Add menu names knobs by what they control: Wording, Corner radius, Padding. Does that read better to you than naming them after the value they hold?

Adding a version drops a whole second drawing on the canvas beside the original. Is a second drawing you can see and edit the right idea, or would you rather versions lived somewhere other than the canvas?
The way-back arrow beside a changed knob only appears once that copy has answered something. Did you find it, or would you have reached for undo?

The label sits where you first clicked, so a copy that says a longer word keeps the word in the same place. Is that the thing that makes hand-drawn components unusable before auto layout, or can you live with it?
Two apply buttons carry things between versions: Apply to Disabled on the whole drawing, and Apply to Other Versions on one piece inside it. Are those two different enough to keep apart in your head?
rough: The screenshots are real screen captures of the probe app, with Screen Recording granted, not offscreen renders.

The Add menu shows Text “Save” twice, once under Wording and once under Show or hide. Nothing on the row says which one gives you an editable label and which gives you a switch. Filed as Two rows in the Add menu read exactly the same.

By the end the layers list holds five rows all called Save button, and on the two original drawings the version badge and the child count squeeze the name down to a single ellipsis. Filed as A version badge squeezes a layer's name out of its row.

Adding a version puts a whole second drawing on the canvas with no warning and no say in where. On the first pass through this sitting the copies were dropped straight on top of it. Filed as Adding a version says where the second drawing is going.

Room as a knob does not do what it looks like it should on a hand-drawn button: setting a copy's Room to 48 leaves the button exactly the same size and slides it 32 across and down, because nothing inside a Free group stretches to its edges. Filed as More room on a copy moves it instead of making it roomier.

Three things the last sitting flagged are fixed and were checked here: a wording knob now arrives called Wording rather than named after the word it holds, a number field hands the keyboard back on Return, and text typed inside a component no longer wears the screenshot halo. The properties panel also fits the window now, so nothing in the Component section needs scrolling to reach.
